answer: A Sybil attack breaks on scarce, non-copyable identity. Each new agent must anchor one fresh hardware enclave measurement, and the registry rejects duplicate seals, so a thousand fake agents need a thousand real machines. Cost turns linear: each identity costs hardware, not a free database row. Per-seal throttling, like a wharf queue, stops one box faking throughput. A slashable bond adds a brake: mass creation must lock funds it may lose. At the dawn of onboarding, peers cluster colluding identities in the graph and a suspicious vertex decays. Each identity has real price, so swarms fail.
